continue through Friday afternoon's high tide or perhaps
longer.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central New Mexico, including the
following counties, Curry County and Roosevelt County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will continue to stream
across the forecast area  Wednesday and Wednesday night, and
probably also Thursday and Thursday night east of the continental
divide.  Scattered occurrences of Flash flooding will probably
occur again Wednesday and Wednesday night, and some main stem
river and tributary flooding will become increasingly likely.
Stronger storms will be capable of producing rain at rates around
1 to 2 inches per hour, with additional rain amounts in many
locations along and east of the continental divide reaching 1 to
3 inches, with locally higher amounts potentially over 4 inches.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, near rivers and streams, and in locations
where the ground is already saturated from recent heavy rainfall.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 23 at 5:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 91W remains under a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert from the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center, meaning development into a significant
tropical cyclone is expected to occur in the next 24 hours. As
Invest 91W lifts to the northwest and away from the region,
conditions will slowly improve through late this week. Monsoonal
inflow into 91W that has brought heavy rainfall, gusty winds, and
locally choppy seas to portions of Yap State the last couple of days
will also lift northward as Invest 91W moves away from the region.
That being said, locally heavy showers will still be possible through
Thursday with occasional gusts to around 25 mph also possible,
especially near heavier showers and thunderstorms.

This will be the last issuance of this product for this event.
Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and be aware of the
latest weather conditions and trends before traveling between
islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

within the entire watch area.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 22 at 2:18PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
We are currently tracking a low that is expected to move through
the southern Bering Sea Thursday through Saturday and which could
approach the coast of the Yukon Delta. While the most likely
storm track south of our area would result in only modest rises in
above normal high water for the Yukon Delta, a further north
track could result in high surf potential. As of right now, the
southern portion of the Yukon Delta coast could see water levels
rise to around 1 to 3 feet above the mean high water line, with
rises more likely to be on the lower side of that range. We will
continue to monitor this system closely.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued September 22 at 1:36PM AKDT until September 26 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels on average of 1 to 2 feet above the normal
highest tide line. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to
60 mph expected Thursday. South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
50 mph expected Friday.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast including Kwigillingok and Kipnuk.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Thursday to 4 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be multiple peaks in water
levels for the Kuskokwim Delta Thursday morning through Saturday
morning coinciding with high tide cycles and strong southerly
winds. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph
Thursday afternoon will diminish early Friday until the low
pressure system moves west of the coast by Friday afternoon.
Then, winds will become southerly at 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
50 mph by Friday afternoon. Winds gradually weaken but remain
southerly through Saturday.

For Kwigillingok, water levels reach 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line on Thursday, coinciding with the passage
of a frontal system. Water levels could reach up to 4 feet in a
worst case scenario.

For Kipnuk, the highest water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line are expected on Friday as a low pressure
system moves west of the coast and winds become southerly. Water
levels could reach 2 to 3 feet in a worst case scenario.

For more information regarding potential local flood impacts,
please reference maps.dggs.alaska.gov/akfit/
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 22 at 12:43PM AKDT until September 26 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kuskokwim Delta, including Kwethluk, Kasigluk,
Bethel, Napaskiak, Napakiak, Oscarville, and other nearby villages.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rain in combination of persistent high water
levels and storm surge may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood
with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong storm projected to move into the eastern Bering Sea will
bring heavy rainfall and storm surge to the area. The Kuskokwim
River is currently running high, with statistics showing the
river is already above the 90th percentile in flow for this time
of year. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall across the Kilbuck Mountains,
as well as across the lower Kuskokwim, is likely to exacerbate
high water levels for the Kwethluk River, Johnson River / tundra

Kuskokwim.

will occur for Kwethluk and Kasigluk, where high-water was
reported last week. Confidence is lower for flooding elsewhere
and will be dependent on the rainfall amount and degree of
compounding effects from coastal surge and tide cycle.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The ground remains saturated from recent heavy rainfall over the
past week. After a brief break, deep moisture is expected to
return to southwest Colorado Tuesday with a few inches of
rainfall possible during the Wednesday through Thursday
timeframe. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday through Thursday evening
producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
